title: Replace quadratic removed-run membership scans with one current-ID set under the test-run rescan lock
outcome: Replace only the nested removed-ID membership scan in test-run rescan with a scoped HashSet<&str>; retain publication, rollback, ordering and durability behavior. This is a source-derived complexity reduction within the measured lock holder, not a live speedup or parent root-cause closure.
acceptance: Removed-run detection in the production test-run rescan builds current-ID membership once and checks each previous ID once, replacing the nested linear scan with expected O(M+N) membership work; only membership detection changes, while the previous-entry map, changed/restored handling, existing removal sort, rollback, cards and compaction remain unchanged.

Deterministic tests prove identical removed IDs for empty, unchanged, reordered, added, removed, duplicate-current, case-sensitive and prefix-distinct IDs; integration controls retain sorted removal publication, first-directory selection for duplicate IDs, and previous entries after unsent delta failures. These are semantic controls, not a manufactured failing functional RED or a wall-clock benchmark.

The exact input passes the authorized focused checks and full gate, receives independent read-only Codex plus Kimi review with recorded Claude unavailability and no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding, and passes independent acceptance before completion.

Evidence reports this slice as a code-derived complexity reduction within the measured rescan lock region; it does not claim the live population, the runtime fraction saved, the full registration-deadline cause, or closure of the parent persistence incident without separate measurement.
